pr_title: Allow `ActiveJob::Base.set` to configure jobs when using `.perform_now`
pr_body:
### Summary

Closes #43376, to allow `ActiveJob::Base.set` to configure jobs using `perform_now`.

Extracts an instance method, `#set` (symmetrically named to the class method `.set`) that extracts the configuration assignment options embedded in `#enqueue`.

As discussed in #43376, this behavior is necessary because:

- Existing enqueue options may be relevant to a `.perform_now` job that has a `retry_on` handler.
- ActiveJob extensions may add additional configuration options that should be accessible to `.perform_now`.
pr_comments:
@ghiculescu `.perform_later` already has this behavior. The implementation is slightly different because `#enqueue` already accepts those options as an argument. 

I can go a few directions, do you have a preference?

- Have `ConfiguredJob#perform_later`'s implementation use the new `ActiveJob::Base#set` method and not use `ActiveJob::Base#enqueue`'s options. This would make the ConfiguredJob's implementation symmetrical. 
- Have `ActiveJob::Base#perform_now` accept options as an argument, which would make its interface symmetrical with `ActiveJob::Base#enqueue`.
Oh sorry I missed that `@options` is passed in as an argument to `enqueue`, I think that's fine.

issue_context.title: ActiveJob::Base.set doesn't configure jobs when using perform_now
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

```ruby
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = :async

class MyJob < ActiveJob::Base
  queue_as :default

  def perform
    puts queue_name
  end
end
```

When using `set().perform_now`, the options passed to `set` are not retrievable in the job instance:

```ruby
> MyJob.set(queue: :another_queue).perform_now
Performing MyJob (...) from Async(default) enqueued at
default
Performed MyJob (...) from Async(default) in 0.29ms
```

### Expected behavior

The behavior is expected to be the same when using `perform_now` or `perform_later` on a configured job.


```ruby
> MyJob.set(queue: :another_queue).perform_later
Enqueued MyJob (...) to Async(another_queue)
Performing MyJob (...) from Async(another_queue) enqueued at 2021-10-05...
another_queue
Performed MyJob (...) from Async(another_queue) in 0.26ms

> MyJob.set(queue: :another_queue).perform_now
Performing MyJob (...) from Async(another_queue) enqueued at
another_queue
Performed MyJob (...) from Async(another_queue) in 0.29ms
```

It might seem useless because the job is performed synchronously, but it's not when building complex jobs flows, which is mixing `perform_now` and` perform_later` methods, in the same given queue.


```ruby
class MyJob < ActiveJob::Base
  queue_as :default

  def perform
    if something_is_not_ready?
      MyJob.set(queue: queue_name, wait: 1.minute).perform_later
    else
      ...
      MyOtherJob.set(queue: queue_name).perform_now
    end
  end
end
```

### System configuration

Rails 6.1.4.1
Also reproductible in master


### Solution proposal

I'll propose the following suggestion in a coming PR :

```ruby
module ActiveJob
  class ConfiguredJob
    ...

    def perform_now(...)
      instantiate(...).perform_now
    end

    def perform_later(...)
      instantiate(...).enqueue
    end

    private

    def instantiate(...)
      job = @job_class.new(...)
      self.class.configure(job, @options)
    end

    def self.configure(job, options = {})
      job.scheduled_at = options[:wait].seconds.from_now.to_f if options[:wait]
      job.scheduled_at = options[:wait_until].to_f if options[:wait_until]
      job.queue_name   = self.class.queue_name_from_part(options[:queue]) if options[:queue]
      job.priority     = options[:priority].to_i if options[:priority]
      job      
    end
  end

  module Enqueuing
    def enqueue(options = {})
      ActiveJob::ConfiguredJob.configure(self, options)
      ...
    end
  end
end
```
comments:
From the example I still don't understand the reason of passing options to `perform_now` when all the possible options are only related to enqueueing logic.

Can you elaborate this further?

In a complex workflow, I have jobs which will launch other jobs, which will launch other jobs, etc ... 

Each child job can be performed independently of the others.
In some conditions, I'll start the whole workflow, in others, I'll just need a child job to be performed.

If I decide to start the workflow in a specific queue, all child jobs have to be performed in the same queue, regardless of the default `queue_as`

When a job is poped out of the queue to be performed, I would prefer to perform all the child jobs in one shot instead of enqueueing multiple jobs (especially if my queue is always full of thousands other jobs).

But if some conditions are not met, I'll delay the execution of the job.
I also use [activejob-uniqueness](https://github.com/veeqo/activejob-uniqueness) to ensure that some of the child jobs are performed without concurency

```ruby
class WorkflowJob < BaseJob
  queue_as :default

  def perform
    AJob.set(queue: queue_name).perform_now
    BJob.set(queue: queue_name).perform_now
    CJob.set(queue: queue_name).perform_now
    ...
  end
end

class AJob < BaseJob
  queue_as :default

  def perform
    return enqueue(queue: queue_name, wait: 5.minutes) if prerequisite_are_not_ready?
    ...
  end
end

class BJob < BaseJob
  queue_as :default

  unique :until_and_while_executing, on_runtime_conflict: ->(job) { job.enqueue(queue: queue_name, wait: 1.hour) }

  def perform
    ...
  end
end

> WorkflowJob.set(queue: 'high_priority').perform_later
# Enqueued WorkflowJob (...) to Async(high_priority)
# Performing WorkflowJob (...) to Async(high_priority)
# Performing AJob (...) to Async(default)
# > Prerequisite for AJob are not ready
# Enqueued AJob (...) to Async(default)
# Performing BJob (...) to Async(default)
# > Another BJob is running
# Enqueued BJob (...) to Async(default)
```

ActiveJob::ConfiguredJob is already providing the `perform_now`.
I think it's relevant to configure the job whether you decide to perform it now or later.

I'm the maintainer of GoodJob and I support this change. 

ActiveJob extensions/plugins (and adapters) will use `set` options to track additional job metadata. And consistency across `perform_now` and `perform_later` would be nice, as `perform_now` operations can flow into `perform_later`s.

An example of that:

```ruby
class MyJob < ActiveJob::Base
  retry_on StandardError, wait: :exponentially_longer, attempts: 2
  
  def perform
    raise "oops"
  end
end

MyJob.set(queue_name: :my_queue).perform_now
```

The intended behavior is that the job will run once immediately in the current context, but if it errors, I'd like it to be retried in the background _on the queue (or priority, etc.) of my choosing at perform time_. Being consistent about `set` would ensure that this behavior works, and enable more complex behavior too.
I made a PR to address this Issue: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/43434
